key_insight: Open-source thigh muscle MRI segmentation tools vary widely in performance, with domain-specific models generally outperforming foundation and general-purpose architectures.
clinical_relevance: Better segmentation can improve MRI-derived muscle biomarkers used in neuromuscular disease research and monitoring, but poor performance on pathology may limit real-world reliability.
method: Tested on 3D MRI volumes from three base datasets and derived datasets
Compared both quantitative accuracy and qualitative usability
evidence_signal: The study reports substantial performance differences across methods and datasets, with reduced accuracy on pathological cases.
watch_item: Results may not generalize well to underrepresented populations or disease presentations, so local validation is important before deployment.
paper_title: Benchmarking open-source automated thigh muscle MRI segmentation algorithms
